committee_name.text: FDA Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee

quote.quote: FDA Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee Meeting was held on March 19, 2009 to discuss NDA 22-406 Xarelto (rivaroxaban) oral tablet 10 mg for the proposed indication.
FDA Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee Meeting was held on March 19, 2009 to discuss NDA 22-406 Xarelto (rivaroxaban) oral tablet 10 mg for the proposed indication.

recommendation.text: The committee voted 15 (yes) to 2 (no) that the available clinical data demonstrate a favorable risk-benefit profile for rivaroxaban in VTE prophylaxis after hip or knee replacement surgery. A separate question on whether a lower dose than 10 mg should be available for special populations was voted 5 (yes) to 9 (no), 3 abstain.

quote.quote: The Committee voted 15 (yes) to 2 (no) that the available clinical data demonstrate a favorable risk-benefit profile for rivaroxaban in the prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing hip or knee replacement surgery.

linkages.concern: Committee members raised concern about the strength of the hepatotoxicity signals and the feasibility of long-term studies to further characterize the liver injury potential, and most members stated that longer-term studies are needed.
linkages.change: The application was not approved in the first cycle; the review team required additional long-term follow-up safety (liver) data from the ongoing ROCKET atrial-fibrillation studies, which the sponsor supplied in the resubmission before approval.

concern_quote.quote: committee members expressed varying levels of concern about the strength of the signals for hepatotoxicity and the feasibility of long term studies to further elucidate the hepatotoxicity seen with rivaroxaban

change_quote.quote: The review team requested additional long term follow-up data from the ROCKET studies where rivaroxaban was used for stroke prophylaxis in patients with atrial fibrillation.

linkages.concern: On the question of whether a lower dose than 10 mg should be available for special populations, the committee voted against it (5 yes to 9 no, 3 abstain), with many members saying there was not enough data to support a lower dose.
linkages.change: The approval used a single 10 mg daily dose for all patients; no lower-strength dose was approved for special populations.

concern_quote.quote: the committee voted 5 (Yes) to 9 (No) (abstain 3). Many committee members expressed that there was not enough data to support a lower dose

change_quote.quote: A single dose of 10 mg daily is recommended for all patients.

summary: An FDA Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee met on March 19, 2009 (first review cycle) and voted 15-2 that the data showed a favorable benefit-risk profile for rivaroxaban in VTE prophylaxis after hip or knee replacement surgery; no advisory committee was convened for the 2011 resubmission that led to approval. The committee's main concern was the strength of the hepatotoxicity signal and the need for longer-term data, and the review team required additional long-term liver safety data from the ROCKET atrial-fibrillation studies, which (together with DSI data-integrity findings) resulted in a first-cycle Complete Response and approval only after the resubmission. The committee also voted against making a lower dose available for special populations, and the product was approved at a single 10 mg daily dose; both linkages are inferred because the review documents describe the concerns and the changes but do not explicitly state the causal connection.
